title: Ordering and paying
summary: Requests, payment forms and currency amounts: 1, 2–4 and 5+.

water.note: Accusative: what is brought takes the accusative.

card.sentenceGloss: We will pay for dinner by card.
card.note: Instrumental: заплатити takes the instrumental for the means of payment.

cash.sentenceGloss: Today we are paying in cash.
cash.note: Instrumental: платити takes the instrumental for the means of payment.

coffee.sentenceGloss: I will order coffee without milk.
coffee.note: Accusative: what is ordered takes the accusative.

one.sentenceGloss: There is one hryvnia on the table.
one.note: Nominative singular: one agrees with the noun in the nominative singular.

two.note: Nominative plural: two takes the plural form of the noun.

five.sentenceGloss: They charged five hryvnias for the napkins.
five.note: Genitive plural: after five the noun is in the second case plural.

twentyone.note: Nominative singular: after a compound numeral ending in одна, the noun agrees with одна — двадцять одна гривня (but двадцять дві гривні).

twentytwo.note: Nominative plural: the last part of the compound agrees with the noun.

twentyfive.note: Genitive plural: after twenty-five the noun is in the second case plural.

bill-request.sentenceGloss: Please give us the bill for dinner.
bill-request.note: Accusative: what is asked for takes the accusative.
